# Restore never returns rail widths: the topology diff skips edge zones

## Context

Found while falsifying the mechanism **my own** #18553 prescribed. That ticket asserts the `topologyFingerprint` answers "have you left the default layout". I ran the falsifier instead of taking the assertion, and the fingerprint turned out to be shape-only — which led to the differ beside it, which turned out to be blind on a first-class gesture.

This is #18255 one axis over. That ticket found the diff had no active-item category, so a restore *"brings the tabs back, but not the tab you were on"*. Its body lists what the planner emits — `addTab`, `moveItem`, `resizeSplit`, `setItemAutoHidden` — and `resizeEdgeZone` is absent from that list. Nobody, including me reading it today, noticed the second omission.

Live latest-open sweep: latest 20 open issues at `2026-09-10T11:50:28Z`; no equivalent found. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last 30 messages: no claim on this scope. Memory Core rationale sweep on the observed symptom returned only the #17845 / #17849 splitter *drag-bounds* work (live clamp semantics), a different layer with no decision touching this. Own-assignment sweep: 14 open, none on the dock diff/planner surface.

## The Problem

Measured at `dev@2fdc57af69`, against the real `apps/workstation/tour/denseWorkstation.mjs` `initialDocument`, applying real `Operations` and reading both instruments:

| user operation | change class | shape fingerprint | `diffDockDocuments` |
|---|---|---|---|
| drag the main split 0.6/0.4 → 0.25/0.75 | `geometry` | unchanged | `resizes` |
| **drag the left rail 0.11 → 0.4** | `geometry` | unchanged | **NOTHING** |
| switch the active tab | `topology` | unchanged | `activeItemChanges` |
| reorder a tab in place | `topology` | unchanged | `tabReorders` |
| lock a pane | `itemFlags` | unchanged | NOTHING |
| relocate a pane across nodes | `topology` | changed | `moves` |
| close a pane | `topology` | changed | `removes` |

The rail drag is the only *layout* gesture no instrument sees. And because `RestorePlanner.planRestore` is a pure fold over that diff, the consequence is not a missing report — it is a silent no-op restore. Same document pair, only the left rail differing:

```
captured left extent : 0.11
live left extent     : 0.4
documents differ     : true
deferred             : false (null)
errors               : []
plan                 : []
```

`deferred: false`, `errors: []`, `plan: []` — the planner reports **success with nothing to do**. A consumer folding that plan concludes the layout is already restored. So a user who widens a rail, saves nothing, and restores a saved perspective gets every pane back at the captured position and the rail left where they dragged it, with no error anywhere.

`initialDocument` marks three of four edges `resizable: true`, so this is the shipped flagship's own configuration, not a corner case.

## The Architectural Reality

The node walk in `diffDockDocuments` examines exactly two node types and returns before reaching the third:

```js
// src/dashboard/dock/model/TopologyDiff.mjs:182
if (beforeNode?.type !== 'split' || afterNode?.type !== 'split') return;
```

`edge-zone` nodes are therefore never inspected, and `extent` lives on the **descriptor**, not the node it points at — `WorkspaceDocument.dockZoneDescriptorKeys = new Set(['nodeId', 'extent', 'resizable'])`, validated finite in the open interval `(0, 1)`. So the value is durable committed document state that the differ structurally cannot reach.

The asymmetry is not a considered contract. `Operations.operationChangeClass` classes the two resize verbs identically:

```js
// src/dashboard/dock/model/Operations.mjs:93-94
resizeSplit   : 'geometry',
resizeEdgeZone: 'geometry',
```

One of that pair is reported and one is not, and no comment anywhere argues that an edge extent is runtime-only — the capture format keeps it, which is the opposite argument. That is the same reasoning #18255 used to establish the active item was unaddressed rather than declined.

Downstream, `RestorePlanner` maps each category to its operation at `:123-129` (`setActiveItem`, `resizeSplit`, `setItemAutoHidden`). There is no arm to add `resizeEdgeZone` to, because the category it would read does not exist.

Two consumers inherit this, not one:

- `persistence/RestorePlanner.mjs:71` — every perspective restore.
- `src/ai/client/DockService.mjs:243` — the Neural Link `diff_dock_topology` MCP tool, whose JSDoc already scopes its tolerance to *"split size fractions"*. An agent asking what changed after a rail drag is told nothing changed.

**A stale docblock is part of this.** `TopologyDiff`'s class comment enumerates seven categories; the code returns eight — `activeItemChanges`, added by #18255, was never added to the prose. Hand-copying that list from the docblock under-reported the `setActiveItem` row in my first measurement pass, which is how a category omission stays invisible to the next reader.

## The Fix

- `TopologyDiff.diffDockDocuments` gains an edge-zone extent category, in the same `{nodeId, ...}` shape as the existing ones — the walk stops short-circuiting on `edge-zone` and compares each zone descriptor's `extent` under the same epsilon discipline `resizes` already uses.
- `RestorePlanner.planRestore` emits `resizeEdgeZone` for each, ordered with the other geometry steps (after adds/moves/reorders — geometry applies to a settled tree).
- The class docblock's category list is brought back into agreement with what the code returns, `activeItemChanges` included.

Nothing new in the model: `Operations.resizeEdgeZone` is already implemented, registered and classed. This is a diff category and one plan step, exactly the shape #18255 landed.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TopologyDiff.diffDockDocuments` result | `model/TopologyDiff.mjs:103` `empty()` | one added category array, additive; existing categories byte-identical | absent/malformed `zones` fails closed through the existing shape gate, as today | class docblock category list, corrected to match the code | probe table above; existing `DockTopologyDiff.spec.mjs` must stay green unchanged |
| `sizeEpsilon` option | `diffDockDocuments({sizeEpsilon})`, `SIZE_EPSILON = 0.001` | reused for extents — both are fractions in `(0, 1)`, so one tolerance stays honest; a second knob would be a contract nobody asked for | omitted → `SIZE_EPSILON`, as today | JSDoc drops "on split size fractions" | `dockZoneDescriptorKeys` validates `extent` in the same open interval as split sizes |
| `RestorePlanner.planRestore` plan | `persistence/RestorePlanner.mjs:114-129` | may now contain `resizeEdgeZone` steps | a document with no edge zones plans exactly as today | planner ordering comment | `Operations.operationChangeClass:94` already classes the verb |
| `diff_dock_topology` MCP tool | `src/ai/client/DockService.mjs:17,243` | reports the new category; no signature change | unchanged | tool JSDoc | pass-through call site, no local shaping |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — A document pair differing only in one edge-zone `extent` produces a non-empty diff naming that zone. Red-first: the arm pins today's empty result and flips.
- [ ] **AC-2** ⚠️ **The planner arm is the one that matters.** `planRestore(dragged, captured)` emits a `resizeEdgeZone` step; today it returns `deferred: false, errors: [], plan: []` and that triple is what makes the defect silent. An arm asserting only the diff category leaves the user-visible half unwitnessed.
- [ ] **AC-3** — Round trip: applying the emitted plan returns the live document's extent to the captured value.
- [ ] **AC-4** — Sub-epsilon extent drift reports **no** change, matching `resizes`. Restore plans stay minimal; a no-op step is a spurious commit.
- [ ] **AC-5** — A zone whose descriptor carries no `extent` on one or both sides emits no step and no error; absence is not a change to zero.
- [ ] **AC-6** ⚠️ **`resizable` is not extent.** A descriptor whose `resizable` flag differs but whose `extent` matches emits no resize step — the fix must not smuggle a policy flag into a geometry category.
- [ ] **AC-7** — Every existing `DockTopologyDiff.spec.mjs` and `DockRestorePlanner.spec.mjs` arm stays green **unmodified**. The category is additive; a spec that had to be edited to pass means the shape changed.
- [ ] **AC-8** — Mutation-verified: removing the diff emit reds AC-1 and AC-2; removing the planner emit reds AC-2 alone, so the two arms are shown to cover different failures.
- [ ] **AC-9** — The `TopologyDiff` class docblock enumerates exactly the categories the code returns, `activeItemChanges` included. The drift is what hid this omission from its own readers.

## Out of Scope

`setItemLocked` invisibility — the diff has no lock category either, but locking is an item policy rather than a layout geometry, and whether a restore should re-apply it is a question nobody has asked. Measured here and deliberately left: a separate finding, not a silent fold-in.

The `computeShapeFingerprint` blindness itself. Shape-only is that function's documented and correct contract — it is the guardrail for `windowFingerprint`, and widening it would break the equality it exists to provide. #18553 stops prescribing it; the fingerprint does not change.

Live drag bounds and clamp semantics (#17845 / #17849 lineage). This is the model/plan tier, not the interactive resize tier.

## Avoided Traps

⚠️ Do not solve this consumer-side. Three call sites read this differ; a consumer-side extent comparison in #18553's indicator would leave `RestorePlanner` and the MCP tool exactly as broken, and would hand-write in the app what the model already owns.

⚠️ Do not fold extents into the existing `resizes` array. Its entries carry `fromSizes`/`toSizes` arrays keyed by split node; an edge zone changes one scalar on one keyed zone of a node. Reusing the array forces consumers to type-sniff entries, and `RestorePlanner` maps category → operation one-to-one — a mixed array breaks that mapping.

⚠️ Do not widen the shape fingerprint to notice extents so the gate catches it. `planRestore` uses shape equality to decide *whether the topologies are comparable at all*; making a rail drag a shape mismatch would turn an ordinary restore into a `topology-fingerprint-mismatch` deferral.

⚠️ Do not read the class docblock as the category list. It is stale by one, which is precisely how this stayed unseen — derive categories from the returned object.
